title: Ethiopian Vegetable Stew with Berbere
localName: አትክልት ወጥ ቤርቤሬ — Atkilit Wat be-Berbere
community: All of Ethiopia — the spiced mixed vegetable wat
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Spiced Mixed Vegetable Stew — a mix of seasonal vegetables (eggplant, potato, carrot, bell pepper, tomato) cooked in a berbere sauce. The spiced version of the mixed vegetable wat — for those who want all the heat of berbere in their vegetables.
longDesc: Spiced mixed vegetable wat applies the full berbere tradition to whatever vegetables are seasonally available — eggplant absorbs the sauce beautifully, potatoes thicken it, and the carrots and peppers add colour and nutrition.
steps: Cook onions until golden. Add berbere. Fry 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes and bell pepper. Cook 4 minutes.
Add potatoes and carrots. Add water. Cover. Cook 12 minutes.
Add eggplant. Cover. Cook 10 more minutes.
chefTips: Add eggplant last — it cooks faster than root vegetables.
Salt eggplant to prevent it absorbing excessive oil.
cookingScience: See ETH125 for eggplant science. The combination of vegetables produces a self-thickening sauce — potato starch and dissolved eggplant flesh create a natural thickener without any added starch.
sustainabilityTips: Use whatever is seasonal and available.
culturalNote: The spiced mixed vegetable wat adapts Ethiopian berbere cooking to whatever is available — the principle that the berbere tradition can be applied to any vegetable is one of Ethiopian cuisine's great flexibilities.
